sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The primitive scores are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. BQS is 5.58, displayed 5.6; GQS is 6.55, displayed 6.6. Both have 100% factor coverage. IAS is NS: coverage is 45%, known contribution 1.995 and missing-factor bounds 2.545–7.495, not a rankable midpoint. IAS Q uses unrounded final BQS of 5.58, not displayed 5.6.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8% and EXEC 8%. GQS uses REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15% and CASH 10%. IAS uses Q 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10% and L 10%. Exact Decimal contributions are embedded. Missing R/P/L are not imputed or renormalized. REV begins at 9 for three-year CAGR above 30% and caps at 8 for history/confidence, with no second small-base penalty. CAP 6 uses the coherent organic incremental-return bridge; private cohort data are not mandatory. A CAP 7 alternative yields BQS 5.70 and GQS 6.70, while CAP 5 yields 5.46/6.40. This judgment range does not cure IAS missingness or the G2/G4 holds. No numerical governance, funding or persistent-poor-cash override is applied.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Kratikal sells Threatcop people-security products through direct and channel sales and performs vulnerability assessment/penetration testing and cyber-compliance services. Threatcop licences generally charge annually per user with tiered modules, often billed in advance; service engagements may be annual asset-based programmes or one-off projects. Therefore neither all revenue nor all contracts should be called recurring SaaS. FY26 TSAT contributed ₹15.8576 crore, TLMS ₹1.6464 crore and TDMARC ₹2.2413 crore; together these products were 53.77% of sales. VAPT ₹12.8418 crore, compliance ₹3.9768 crore, vCISO ₹0.10 crore and AutoSecT ₹0.0519 crore form the balance, subject to rounding. Reported exports were ₹10.9921 crore/29.94%; customers 677 and staff 200. Domestic and export disclosures have minor classification differences across notes, so no invented geographic profit segmentation is used. The US subsidiary Threatcop AI Inc was incorporated in December 2025 and contributed ₹3.1564 crore revenue; UAE entity had no FY26 revenue. Academy activity is immaterial. Promoter-related Threatcop Inc is a different entity from the wholly owned Threatcop AI Inc. No unit-level gross margins, paid-seat counts, retention, NRR or customer-acquisition cost series are disclosed.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: Annual security-awareness workflows, multiple interoperating modules, channel relationships and embedded compliance processes may raise switching effort. The evidence does not yet demonstrate a durable structural moat: customer logos and product names do not establish retention or pricing power, larger international products compete for the same budgets, and VAPT/compliance work is labour intensive. Top customer share rose to 8.93% and top 10 to 31.60% in FY26 from 5.11%/21.89% in FY25. Product mix is improving, but retention and module penetration are unreported. TAC InfoSec is a relevant product-security comparator, reporting FY26 revenue ₹57.26 crore and 88% growth, but its acquired Cyberscope perimeter and different economics prohibit mechanical premium matching. The issuer's own peer table shows AAA Technologies revenue ₹20.3786 crore and Accedere ₹4.1534 crore in FY26, both with different services mix; these are issuer-compiled peer data, not independent peer-audit endorsements. No current peer P/E ladder is fabricated. MOAT 5 reflects useful, contestable products and relationships rather than an assumed global SaaS moat.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Revenue was ₹5.4289 crore in the FY22 standalone comparative, ₹9.1427 crore in FY23 restated consolidated accounts, ₹13.0158 crore in FY24, ₹20.8509 crore in FY25 and ₹36.7159 crore in FY26. The chosen comparable FY23–26 three-year CAGR is 58.95%. The four-year FY22–26 context is 61.26%, but mixes the older standalone comparative and is not substituted to maximise the score. Five- and ten-year comparable endpoints are unavailable. FY24/25/26 annual additions were ₹3.8731/7.8351/15.8650 crore.

FY26 standalone revenue of ₹33.5595 crore implies 60.95% growth. The ₹3.1564 crore US contribution is new greenfield business, not acquired revenue. Client count rose 424→638→677, while revenue per aggregate client rose ₹3.07→3.27→5.42 lakh. FY26 client growth of 6.11% is far below 76.09% revenue growth, indicating spend, mix and new geography rather than demonstrated paid-seat growth. No same-customer cohort bridge is available.

Quarterly FY26 revenue of ₹6.4767/7.0346/10.5075/12.6971 crore shows acceleration and 34.58% Q4 concentration. Comparable FY25 quarters were ₹3.9328/4.9925/5.3272/6.5984 crore. No FY27 interim revenue was verified by the cutoff. June 2025 is not a current quarter, and no invented TTM is used.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway is credible but expensive. IPO objects allocate ₹23.0845 crore to international marketing/workforce and ₹9.2345 crore to product development, leaving ₹2.7151 crore GCP from net proceeds of ₹35.0341 crore. The foreign plan is 26 hires with ₹11.03 crore annual salaries, ₹1.6545 crore initial recruitment fees and ₹10.4 crore initial marketing, scheduled July 2026–June 2027.

The model retains salaries after June 2027, applies 5% annual salary inflation and assumes 50% of initial marketing recurs. It separately tests no additional marketing, half payroll and programme termination. Termination is not a supported base assumption. Existing percentage margins include legacy salaries and marketing, so the separate incremental-cost model is a conservative stress: actual hiring phasing and absorption of new costs within the wider expense base could materially improve outcomes. It is not proof that every new sale bears duplicate costs. Product development is expensed economically and modeled as the greater of recurring development payroll and the IPO budget, avoiding a double charge for the same staff.

Operating and financing invested capital reconcile across FY23–26. The three-year incremental NOPAT/IC proxy is 34.64%, above a reasoned 14–18% capital-cost range, and the full-development-expense sensitivity is 46.97%. Net investment reconciles within ₹0.0001 crore. This coherent organic bridge supports CAP 6 without mandatory private cohort data. It is not a project IRR: legacy margin/utilization improvements and newly incorporated overseas activity affect attribution, while substantial software remains unfinished. These mixed maturities prevent treating the aggregate return as proof that the new programmes will earn the same return. A CAP 7 alternative is shown transparently. Bottom-up customer and staffing requirements at FY26 productivity are embedded for every case; a global market-size narrative does not replace this test.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoters controlled 72.58% before the IPO and 53.36% after it. No pledge was disclosed at the prospectus date; a current pledge update is unverified. FY26 director remuneration was about ₹1.0010 crore, 16.3% of restated PAT.

The prospectus describes old rights/private-placement lapses involving delayed appropriation or filings, valuation documentation and a separate bank-account requirement. Management describes these as procedural/clerical, not willful diversion. Applications were filed on 30 December 2025; the private-placement application was disclosed approved on 8 January 2026, while the rights matter remained pending. A separate consolidated-filing correction/adjudication was disclosed approved on 20 April 2026. These are preserved as disclosed statuses, not independent proof every matter is closed. The audit's private-company section 197 sentence should be reconciled with public conversion on 23 September 2025, without asserting a legal violation.

Promises versus delivery: AutoSecT transferred ₹3.4209 crore to completed software during FY26, yet revenue was only ₹0.0519 crore. Autocode/admin software of ₹8.6308 crore remained unfinished. The international programme deadline of June 2027 had not elapsed at the cutoff, so it is not a missed deadline. The 28 July US order of ₹0.212791 crore is real but explicitly below materiality. The 6 August board authorization of ₹15.97 crore in subsidiary subscriptions is permission, not demonstrated spending. ESOP ratification is not financing. The 42,833 outstanding grants and the total 387,625-option pool stress are distinguished rather than added twice.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Use the latest restated series, not a mixture of accounting versions. FY25 old DRHP PAT of ₹4.2334 crore was superseded by ₹3.8144 crore, principally through an additional ₹0.4190 crore tax provision. FY26 books PAT of ₹5.9608 crore plus tax and deferred-tax adjustments of ₹0.0991 and ₹0.0826 crore equals ₹6.1425 crore. Equity bridges are also disclosed.

The cash differences have important counterevidence. Annual cash of ₹0.5924161 crore plus the positive ICICI OD asset of ₹0.9532151 crore equals the restated ₹1.5456 crore within rounding; FY25 does the same. The FY26 CFO difference of ₹1.16912 crore mechanically bridges through ₹0.82775 crore of gross-capex/DA correction and ₹0.3413932 crore of OD movement. This independent classification bridge is not unexplained missing cash, nor is it an auditor-certified reconciliation. Restated labels of ₹0.9548 crore cash-in-hand and ₹0.0147 crore ICICI OD do not map to statutory hand cash of ₹0.0163092 crore and OD of ₹0.9532151 crore. Availability and sublabels need confirmation.

The unmodified main audit invokes an absent audit-trail paragraph in its proper-books exception, leaving the scope of that exception unknown. IFC reporting is expressly claimed exempt, not separately given a clean opinion. CARO reports no working-capital facilities above ₹5 crore, so its bank reconciliation clause is not an affirmative clean reconciliation. Guarantee wording conflicts, but quantified bank guarantees are only ₹0.0342 crore; indirect-tax and regulatory contingencies add ₹0.0410 crore. Term-loan use wording is inconsistent with the tiny disclosed debt and needs clarification, not an allegation of diversion. No actual fraud or default is asserted.

Three-year CFO/PAT of 0.8281 masks FY26 deterioration to 0.3416. Receivables of ₹8.9197 crore rose 119.5%; closing DSO is 88.7 days and average DSO 64.5 days. Most balances are under six months, with ₹0.1706 crore older than one year. Three-year CFO less development is −₹1.1536 crore before tangible capex; full FCF is −₹2.5432 crore. FY26 development-expensed EBIT of ₹3.9775 crore is a sensitivity, not a corrected audit opinion. IPO holder dilution was 26.49%, distinct from 36.03% share-count expansion. Historical FY26 basic/diluted EPS of ₹7.86/7.85 uses weighted shares, not post-IPO shares.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹152.10 and 11,100,545 shares, market capitalization is ₹168.8393 crore: 27.49× FY26 restated PAT and 56.60× a 25%-taxed, full-development-expense earnings sensitivity. March-based EV/EBITDA is 18.42×, but is stale and excludes subsequent IPO cash; no current October EV is claimed. The principal method is a five-year cash-linked economic-earnings multiple. A perpetual DCF would require unverified software useful lives and steady-state reinvestment economics, so none is forced and no DCF terminal-value share applies.

Base growth is 25/25/22/20/18/15%, pre-development EBIT margin 23–25%, recurring development 12.6% of sales, ONWC 20% and exit P/E 18×. Bear uses 5–8% growth, 18% margin, 14% development, 30% ONWC and 12× P/E. Bull uses growth declining from 40% to 22%, margin rising from 26% to 30%, 12% development, 16% ONWC and 24× P/E. All retain foreign payroll and continued marketing explicitly. Unspent object proceeds are ring-fenced, and operating cash is retained at the terminal date. Required cash after IPO is the greater of ₹1.5 crore or 30 days of cash costs, with a 45-day stress.

The conservative reconstruction starts with lower statutory cash, excludes positive OD and FD balances, recoups ₹0.7208 crore of prepaid IPO costs once, settles net legacy tax/statutory dues once and repays ₹0.005 crore debt. At the October entry, base modeled cash is ₹28.0124 crore, of which ₹22.6488 crore remains earmarked; unrestricted headroom over the required reserve is ₹2.2856 crore. At March 2027, base headroom is ₹4.5593 crore. The first base continuation gap is during July 2027–March 2028. These are assumption-based reconstructions, not published cash balances.

All three full-continuation paths later breach reserves, so ordinary and non-rescue conditional returns/entry prices remain null. Separate beginning-period equity rescue at ₹121.68 with 3% fees raises about ₹76.59/45.69/11.22 crore in bear/base/bull. Base and bear remain economically loss-making at exit; P/E valuation is NM, not an asserted zero liquidation value. Bull rescue gives an illustrative IRR of about 0.26%, with about 8.0% total holder dilution including existing options. This is neither available financing nor an ordinary return estimate. Changing cost absorption or hiring plans can materially change the result.

The canonical includes growth× multiple, working-capital, development, object-overrun/tax, FD release, fee-credit, ESOP, payroll/marketing and 12/15/18% hurdle sensitivities, plus rescue discount/fee tests. Reverse expectations reject unfunded brackets and report no feasible crossing, never a search endpoint as a required-growth solution. No ordinary valuation range is supplied.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear argument is that a small profitable domestic product/services business is funding a much more expensive international selling model before proving its customer economics. If new contracts require high acquisition spending and receivables rise faster than revenue, profit can coexist with negative owner cash. Capitalized software may require amortization or impairment if new products fail; it is not liquid collateral.

The explicit continuation stress needs capital even in the bull case. Negative economic profits make a P/E terminal recovery unreliable in bear and base. Discounted equity with issue fees dilutes existing holders; larger discounts worsen the result, and actual funding may be unavailable. Counterevidence matters: almost no debt, a real IPO raise, mostly current receivables, strong organic growth and the ability to adjust uncommitted hiring/campaigns. Thus this is not proof of actual default or inevitable distress. The decisive variables are overseas contribution after payroll/marketing, cash after development and current liquidity. Neither a clean main audit opinion nor an incomplete invoked audit-trail paragraph alone settles the economic or integrity question.

sections.title: 5× and10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome over five years requires 37.97% CAGR; tenfold requires 58.49%. These are not revenue growth requirements because margins, dilution and valuation multiples intervene. A mechanical 18× P/E and 9.3% after-tax economic-margin test, before cash and dilution, requires roughly ₹504 crore revenue for 5× and ₹1,009 crore for 10× versus ₹36.72 crore in FY26. That simplified margin excludes the separately modeled continuing foreign cost and is not a conservative forecast.

Customer and staff productivity tests show the capacity required for the modeled terminal scale; cohort data are missing. No evidenced 5×/10× path or probability is assigned. Global cybersecurity TAM alone does not make either outcome financeable.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain the complete corrected signed audit-trail paragraph, clarify IFC/section 197 wording, cash labels and CARO loan/guarantee statements. Resolve the material scope issue before a favorable classification.
2. Reconcile IPO utilization to ₹35.0341 crore net objects plus prepaid recoupment, subsidiary cash and external spending. Intra-group subscriptions are not expenses.
3. Track actual overseas headcount against 26 and annual salary run-rate against ₹11.03 crore. Require a post-June 2027 funding/P&L plan before assuming payroll can continue.
4. Track customer cohorts, ARR/NRR, churn, CAC payback and gross margins separately for products and services. Do not automatically apply a SaaS multiple.
5. Monitor receivables against ₹8.9197 crore, closing DSO of 88.7 days and balances older than one year of ₹0.1706 crore. DSO persistently above 100 days or ageing without collection is a warning.
6. Compare CFO/PAT against FY26 0.342 and three-year 0.828. Sustained conversion below 0.6 warrants material reassessment.
7. Track unfinished software of ₹8.6308 crore and annual development of ₹4.6296 crore. Require commercial revenue and payback, not capitalization alone.
8. Check quarterly revenue concentration, Q4 collections and export profit rather than extrapolating the small first-US order.
9. Verify ESOP grants/exercises, promoter pledge, RPTs and pending remediation outcomes.
10. Obtain official 60-session BSE turnover, spreads, lot and restrictions before implementation analysis.
These are research conditions, not automated buy/sell instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. This is an expansion-stage cybersecurity product/services thesis, not a validated compounder, established deep-value opportunity or proven fraud case. BQS 5.58 (display 5.6) and GQS 6.55 (display 6.6) are complete quality estimates. IAS remains NS and is not investment-rankable. Quality ranks must preserve the reliability/tradability holds rather than imply purchase eligibility. G1 and G3 are Conditional, preserving management explanations and real IPO funding. G2 and G4 holds prevent an implementation conclusion. An ordinary valuation range is withheld, not set to zero.

A lower price can improve prospective economics but cannot establish audit completeness, overseas returns or tradability. The most valuable new evidence is a corrected audit, cash/proceeds bridge, actual hiring costs and overseas cohort contribution after development and marketing. If the broader percentage cost base absorbs new staff and retention economics are strong, the separate-cost stress could be too harsh. If full additional costs persist without revenue acceleration, funding or downsizing could impair minority returns. This is general research, not personalized investment advice or a trading instruction.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger links the 3 July 2026 final prospectus, 22 June RHP, complete FY26 annual report and original signed statutory package, older annual statements, FY23 DRHP history, August board authorization, July US order and official security master. Original PDFs, HTML, OCR and images stay local. Analytical backups retain financial-only extracts, source URLs/digests, code and results. Offline reproduction checks calculations and internal consistency, not fresh authentication of original evidence.

Fact, management assertion, inference and forecast assumption are distinguished in the evidence register. Principal open questions: what did the invoked h(vi) paragraph say; how do cash/OD categories map and which are unrestricted; what is actual IPO utilization and foreign headcount; how much ongoing cost is absorbed within the legacy expense base; what are new-product and customer-cohort returns; and what are current BSE restrictions and execution conditions? Small quantified contingencies and mechanically bridged aggregate cash differences are not described as unexplained missing money.

Model assumptions include 25% cash tax without monetized loss benefits, ₹0.005 crore historical debt repaid, all development expensed economically, optional ESOP cash only on modeled exercise, a 30-day reserve with 45-day stress, no FD release except explicit sensitivity, and no extra property/subsidiary valuation. Tax assets and legacy taxes, prepaid IPO fees, gratuity and NCI are each treated once. The conservative separate-cost model is not evidence that future payroll is irrevocably contracted. Source and scoring limitations are part of the conclusion.
